To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

pulmonary ventilation and pulmonary oxygenation are responsible for increasing pulmonary vascular resistance, for abolishing foramen ovale shunting, for abolishing ductus arteriosum shunting, and for increasing descending aortic blood flow at birth in sheep.
pulmonary ventilation and pulmonary oxygenation are the main determinants of pulmonary blood flow and of the central blood flow patterns that are present at birth.
the effects of fetal lung distension and spontaneous fetal breathing on fetal hemodynamics are: (1) an increase in pulmonary blood flow and (2) an increase in descending aortic blood flow.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the fetal circulation and the mechanisms that regulate fetal and postnatal cardiac output.
the mechanisms that regulate fetal and postnatal blood flow.
the mechanisms by which the cardiovascular system of the fetus responds to birth and to the events that accompany the transition from intrauterine to extrauterine life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fetal cardiovascular system is well adapted to the demands imposed by the fetal state.
the fetal lung is not essential for the increase in cardiac output that occurs at birth.
fetal breathing is a major determinant of the hemodynamic changes at birth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fetal breathing movements and lung expansion are not necessary for increasing cardiac output and for altering central shunts.
the increase in cardiac output after birth is due to the combined effect of increased pulmonary blood flow and an increase in cardiac output per se.
fetal pulmonary ventilation and oxygen uptake are the major stimuli responsible for the birth-related increases in pulmonary blood flow and changes in central blood flow patterns.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fetal lung distension and spontaneous breathing are important for the transition from fetal to postnatal circulation.
the fetus is a highly efficient oxygen consumer, but it does not have to be a highly efficient oxygenator.
fetal lung distension is an important factor that affects hemodynamics at birth.
